note: Files this project's cleaners were ported from. scripts/check-upstream.mjs compares the live content against these hashes; when one moves, re-port the mirror files listed under `mirrors` and update `sha256` in the same commit.
followUp: tests/golden/imageMeta.json and tests/golden/layerA.json hold values generated from `unmark-web`, never from this project's own TypeScript: goldens produced by the code under test assert nothing. If either unmark-web source changed, regenerate as part of the re-port with `npm run regen:golden` (needs a local unmark-web checkout; see UNMARK_WEB_DIR in scripts/regen-golden.mjs), otherwise the tests keep asserting the old behaviour and the drift ships anyway.

sources.comment: Deliberately partial mirror: upstream added BMP, GIF and TIFF in guillaumemeyer/watermarks-remover#107 and unmark-web ports all three, but only GIF is mirrored here — it is the only one of the three that gets uploaded to WordPress in practice. A green check on this source therefore means 'no change we decided to track', not 'byte-for-byte feature parity'. If BMP or TIFF ever matter here, port stripBmp/stripTiff from unmark-web's js/image_meta.js. The ISOBMFF primitives this module exports since unmark-web v0.4.0, and the inspectIsobmff byteScan option added with them, are now mirrored here and used by src/utils/avMeta.ts. byteScan defaults to the previous behaviour, so the image goldens regenerate byte-identical.

Full mirror, both drivers: the buffer driver the golden file pins byte for byte, and the slice driver that walks box and chunk headers through File.slice() so a video is cleaned without being held. Unlike the image port there is no deliberate format gap here; every container unmark-web handles (MP4/MOV/M4A/M4V, WAV, MP3, FLAC) is handled here.
Root source. Changes here land in unmark-web first; this entry catches the window before that happens.

Root source, as above. Deliberately partial mirror: upstream added BMP, GIF and TIFF in guillaumemeyer/watermarks-remover#107 and unmark-web ports all three, but only GIF is mirrored here — it is the only one of the three that gets uploaded to WordPress in practice. A green check on this source therefore means 'no change we decided to track', not 'byte-for-byte feature parity'. If BMP or TIFF ever matter here, port stripBmp/stripTiff from unmark-web's js/image_meta.js. Also partial in a second way since watermarks-remover#156: that change hardened the error handling around the external c2patool subprocess, which has no counterpart in a browser or in this converter. Partial in a third way since watermarks-remover 8e16b822, which passes creationflags=subprocess_creationflags to every subprocess.run so a child process opens no console window on Windows: neither a browser nor this converter starts child processes. Partial in two more ways since 2026-08-27: upstream #252 refuses HTTP redirects in _synthid_score_http to block SSRF, and #254 adds a `changed` field to clean_image's returned dict for clean_file.py's new --only-changed flag. Neither has a counterpart here: this converter makes no HTTP calls, and clean() returns bytes rather than writing a file, so the caller already holds both sides to compare.

Root source. Changes here land in unmark-web first; this entry catches the window before that happens. Partial in one way: inspect_av and clean_av take filesystem paths and use safe_write_bytes, and clean_av re-inspects what it wrote, none of which has a counterpart in a browser. The reporting that re-inspection feeds, including inspection_incomplete, is mirrored. Partial in one more way since upstream #254: clean_av's returned dict gained a `changed` field for clean_file.py's new --only-changed flag. cleanAv here returns the bytes rather than writing a file, so the caller already holds both sides to compare.
